atoms.proposition: the donation is made by an individual to a recognised charity or CASC
the donor has paid at least as much in Income Tax or Capital Gains Tax in the tax year as the amount of Gift Aid being claimed
the donor has made a Gift Aid declaration that gives permission to claim Gift Aid
the donation is not made through Payroll Giving
the donation is not a payment for goods or services or made because the charity or CASC bought goods and services
the donation is not where the donor receives a 'benefit' over a certain limit
the donation is not of shares
the donation is not from a charity card or of vouchers, for example Charities Aid Foundation (CAF) vouchers

decision_target: eligibility for Gift Aid on a donation
limitations: The tax position of the donor and whether a Gift Aid declaration was made are not confirmed and must be verified.
The nature of the £260 donation (e.g., whether it is a payment for goods or services or a benefit) is not definitively established in the scenario and must be assessed based on context.
The policy does not specify how to treat donations where a donor receives a benefit, or whether the benefit threshold applies to non-monetary support.
scope_issues: The policy applies to donations from individuals, but does not specify whether one-off donations or recurring donations are treated differently; this distinction is not addressed in the passages.
